children: Agile Group is nearing a deal with a group of offshore creditors to restructure about $5.183 billion of debt, a move that could help resolve the Chinese property developer's long-running liquidity problems.
A coordination committee representing holders of about 61.5% of its existing syndicated loans is close to finalizing a term sheet and restructuring support agreement, the company said Monday.
Agile expects to launch the restructuring support agreement within six weeks, subject to creditors' internal approvals.
Under the proposed arrangement, creditors would receive about 9.2 billion new Agile shares, representing roughly 64.6% of the company's share capital following the transaction.
The proposal includes senior notes, syndicated loans, perpetual securities, exchangeable bonds and other liabilities owed to creditors by the company.

Agile's debt troubles have unfolded against a prolonged downturn in China's property market. In 2024, the company defaulted on an offshore bond payment, citing liquidity pressure and warning it might be unable to meet its offshore debt obligations.

China's property sector has remained under pressure despite government measures aimed at stabilizing the market, with indebted developers continuing to grapple with weak sales, falling prices and refinancing difficulties.
